items.summary: Add the following stable storage structures to the Motoko backend actor: (1) a stable HashMap keyed by a composite key '(listId#deviceId)' (Text) mapping to a claimed timestamp (Int), persisted via preupgrade/postupgrade hooks into a stable array; (2) a stable HashMap keyed by listId (Text) mapping to an array of used template indices (stable [Nat]), also persisted via preupgrade/postupgrade hooks. These must survive canister upgrades without data loss.

Add an atomic update function `generateComment(listId: Text, deviceId: Text) : async Result<Text, Text>` to the Motoko backend. The function must: (1) check if the composite key '(listId#deviceId)' exists in the claims HashMap — if yes, return Err('Already generated on this device for this list'); (2) find the first template index for the given listId that is NOT in the used-indices set; (3) if no unused index exists, return Err('No comments left for this list'); (4) mark that index as used by inserting it into the per-list used-indices map; (5) insert the claim key into the claims HashMap; (6) return Ok(templateText) where templateText is the template at the selected index (with the list's optional suffix appended if present). The entire operation must be a single update call with no intermediate awaits that could allow a race condition.

Add a query function `getListMetrics() : async [ListMetrics]` to the Motoko backend, where ListMetrics is a record type containing: listId (Text), listName (Text), totalTemplates (Nat), usedTemplates (Nat), availableTemplates (Nat), percentUsed (Float). For each comment list, availableTemplates = totalTemplates - usedTemplates, and percentUsed = usedTemplates / totalTemplates * 100 (return 0.0 if totalTemplates is 0). All values must be calculated dynamically from actual stored data — no hardcoded numbers.

Add a query function `getAvailableCount(listId: Text) : async Nat` to the Motoko backend that returns the number of unused template indices for the given list (totalTemplates - usedIndices.size()). This is used by the frontend to display the dynamic 'Available Comments: N' counter without requiring a full metrics fetch.

In the frontend UserView, redesign the Single Comment Generator section to match the uploaded screenshot exactly: (1) a card with a blue gradient icon (sparkle/star), title 'Single Comment Generator', subtitle 'Generate one comment per list (one per device)'; (2) a 'Select Comment List' dropdown showing only unlocked lists for the selected app/event (keep the existing App/Event selector above it); (3) an 'Available Comments' display box showing the dynamic count fetched from the backend's `getAvailableCount` query for the selected list — the number must reflect real stored data, not a hardcoded value; (4) a lock notice box (blue tinted, with sparkle icon) showing 'You have already generated a comment for this list on this device.' when the device has already claimed a comment from the selected list; (5) a 'Generate Single Comment' button with a blue-to-teal gradient matching the screenshot, disabled (and showing the lock notice) if the device has already claimed a comment from this list. On successful generation, display the generated comment text with a Copy button below the card. On 'No comments left' error, show an 'Out of comments' badge instead.

In the frontend, on app load, ensure a persistent deviceId exists: read from localStorage key 'deviceId'; if missing, generate one via `crypto.randomUUID()` and store it back in localStorage. Pass this deviceId to the `generateComment` backend call. After a successful generation, store the claim in localStorage as a record keyed by listId so the UI can immediately show the lock notice without an extra backend round-trip on re-render.

Add an Admin Metrics section inside the Admin > Comments sub-tab (or as a separate 'Metrics' sub-section within the Admin panel). For each comment list, display a card showing: list name, Total / Used / Available counts (all dynamic from the backend `getListMetrics` query), a horizontal progress bar (Used/Total fill percentage), and a pure SVG/CSS donut chart visualizing Used (filled arc) vs Available (unfilled arc) using stroke-dasharray and stroke-dashoffset on an SVG circle element. No Recharts or other chart library may be added. All numbers must come from real backend data with zero hardcoded values.
